Could you actually live car-light in the Arts District? Mostly for the fun part of the week.

What walks: the core is a handful of blocks along Main Street, roughly Charleston to Colorado. Park once and you can do coffee, lunch, a record shop, galleries and a bar on foot.

posts.title: The property tax on a listing may not be yours
posts.takeaway: Nevada's 3% cap is tied to the owner's primary-residence claim. When you buy, file your own.
posts.cta: Send me an address you're considering and I'll walk you through how the cap works for it before you offer.
posts.ctaNote: Manual service by Mikey. Nothing is automated.

slides.headline: Budgeting with the tax number on a Las Vegas listing?
slides.body: It may not be what you'll pay.
slides.want: Budgeting with the tax number on a Las Vegas listing?

slides.headline: Nevada caps the tax bill increase on a primary residence at 3%.
slides.body: Homes that aren't owner-occupied can see up to 8%.
slides.want: Nevada caps the tax bill increase on a primary residence at 3%.

slides.headline: Clark County: any ownership document recorded removes the owner-occupied 3% abatement.
slides.want: palm-lined street

slides.headline: So the seller's capped bill doesn't carry over.
slides.body: The new owner has to claim the primary residence.
slides.want: So the seller's capped bill doesn't carry over.

slides.headline: Nevada law now puts a claim section on the Declaration of Value filed at closing.
slides.want: Nevada law now puts a claim section on the Declaration of Value filed at closing.

posts.caption:
An easy budgeting mistake on a Las Vegas resale: trusting the tax number on the listing.

Nevada caps the annual increase on a primary residence's tax bill at 3% (NRS 361.4723). Homes that aren't owner-occupied can see up to 8%. The cap is tied to the owner's primary-residence claim: Clark County says any ownership document recorded removes the owner-occupied 3% abatement.

So the seller's capped bill doesn't simply carry over to you. Nevada law now requires a section on the Declaration of Value, filed with the deed at closing, where a new owner can claim it (NRS 375.060). The county also mails new owners a tax cap notice.

Before you trust a listing's tax figure, ask how the cap works for that exact property. Send me the address and I'll walk you through it.
